title: Opioid Safety Edits and the Specialty Pharmacy Requirement
content:
**Clinical edit policy — Pharmacy Benefit.** An opioid fill whose daily MME exceeds the plan's MME daily limit, or a first opioid fill beyond the plan's opioid-naive days supply for a member with no opioid fill in the prior 90 days, rejects with the reject reason "prior authorization required" until approved. Members in hospice or with an active cancer diagnosis on the prescription are exempt; naloxone always pays with no copay. Specialty drugs are filled only at the designated specialty pharmacy where the member's PrairieRx plan requires it.

### Edit table

| Opioid fill | Member in hospice or active cancer diagnosis on the prescription | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Daily MME above the plan's limit | No | Rejected, prior authorization required, until approved |
| Daily MME equal to or below the plan's limit | No | Not rejected by the MME edit |
| First opioid fill (no opioid fill in the prior 90 days) for more days than the plan's opioid-naive days supply | No | Rejected, prior authorization required, until approved |
| First opioid fill for no more than the plan's opioid-naive days supply | No | Not rejected by the first-fill edit |
| Any of the above | Yes | Exempt from these edits |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical, on a plan limit of 90 MME)

- A daily MME of exactly 90 does not exceed the limit and is not rejected by the MME edit.
- A daily MME of 91 exceeds it and is rejected until approved.

### Naloxone and specialty drugs

- Naloxone always pays, with no copay.
- Where the plan requires it, a specialty drug is filled only at the designated specialty pharmacy.
